scope: Seven focused checks execute kernel-mediated bindings, operation authorization, signer entropy and actual same-slot teardown markers in separately installed native Lean probe processes. This is not a Messenger, circuit, mailbox or Ed25519 conformance journey.
source_to_binary: Pinned Lean IR and repository RV64 backend; source-to-binary compiler and complete kernel are not verified. Source files match the frozen source commit byte-for-byte; all three runs load byte-identical guest images and the same identified probe packages.

policy_proofs.scope: Boolean predicates actually used by kernel serviceRightsValid/currentGrant, checked during the clean Lean build; no compiled-binary refinement theorem.

runtime_evidence.host: One development host; AArch64 execution is qemu-aarch64 emulation, not native ARM hardware.

limitations: The wipe test observes controlled nonsecret markers at selected native data, guarded-stack and near/far arena locations; source inspection identifies the complete wipe extent, rather than an exhaustive dump of every byte.
Published signing vectors and signer-only syscall132 permit revocation behavior are qualified separately by the native crypto and Identity journeys.
Kernel cryptographic deadline selection is present in this image but this fast SHA256 entropy probe does not qualify Ed25519 completion latency.
No claims of independent operator ownership, anonymity, constant-time proof, hostile-host isolation or independent security audit are made.
